# data/sfx: jet sound pack v2, combat (generated by `tools/sfx/gen_sfx_combat.py`, tasks A9 + A9b; do not edit)

All files: mono, 22050 Hz, 16-bit PCM, every file peaks at -1 dBFS. Regenerate with
`python3 tools/sfx/gen_sfx_combat.py` (deterministic; `--check` compares md5 with data/), or
`python3 tools/build_assets.py --only sfx` (both sound generators). The v1 flight pack and its engine mix law
are in `README.md` (A5); this file covers only the combat sounds. Loops are seamless: play them with
DSBPLAY_LOOPING from sample 0. Pitch = e_audio `pitch` (rate multiplier of 22050 Hz).

Levels: the *suggested volume* is the e_audio `vol` (before `[sound]` group volumes and the master) that
puts the sound at its designed perceived level on A5's scale: cruise engine about -18 dB, full afterburner
about -11.5 dB, PULL UP (0.55) about -9 dB. `Level` = measured perceived level of the file at vol 1 (band
100 Hz - 6 kHz RMS; loops over the whole loop, one-shots over their loudest 300 ms). Master ~0.7 as in A5.

## The warning tones: how to tell them apart

| Sound | Register | Rhythm | Character |
|---|---|---|---|
| `srm_growl` | low, 400 Hz (pitch up to 500 Hz with signal) | continuous | raspy buzz with waver and flutter |
| `srm_lock` | high, 1600 Hz | continuous | clean steady tone |
| `lock_beep` | high, 1568 -> 2093 Hz | 3 fast pips + held note, once | bright confirmation |
| `rwr_search` | low-mid, 550 -> 470 Hz | one falling 4-step "waterfall" (0.335 s), once | new fighter |
| `rwr_lock` | low-mid, 455/555 Hz | slow two-tone alternation, 2 tones/s (0.25 s each), continuous | calm, insistent |
| `rwr_launch` + `rwr_missile` | low-mid, 455/555 Hz | fast two-tone alternation, 5 tones/s (0.10 s each), continuous | urgent |
| A5 `pullup` | 700 -> 1400 Hz | 2 rising whoops/s | terrain warning |
| A5 `beep` | 1050 Hz | bip-bip, once | message |

Engine bands for reference: fan tone 750-1220 Hz and whine 1980-3230 Hz (they glide with spool). The RWR
tones (user spec, A9b) sit at 455-555 Hz, below the fan band: a clean steady pitch under the engine's
broadband roar, so they stand out by register and by their regular switching (the engine glides, it never
steps). **rwr_lock and rwr_missile use the same two pitches and differ only by rhythm**: 2 tones/s vs 5
tones/s (calm alternation vs fast trill), and rwr_search is a single falling run of 4 pitches. srm_growl
(400-500 Hz) shares the register but is a raspy buzz with flutter, never a clean alternation. Margins in
the tone's 1/3-octave band at the suggested volumes (build log `mask` lines, A9b build), over cruise / over
full afterburner at 700 kt: rwr_missile +18.1 / +12.9 dB, rwr_lock +14.5 / +9.4 dB, rwr_search +12.3 /
+7.2 dB (A5 PULL UP +14.0 / +10.0 dB): the missile tone stays clearly audible in full burner, the lock
tone a bit calmer.
A9's tones are sines with weak low harmonics; the RWR tones are near-pure sines (3rd harmonic -24 dB, 5th
-36 dB) with phase-continuous switches; 3-10 ms raised-cosine attacks/releases (no clicks, no square edge).

## How to play them (snd_combat.cpp, T17)

- **srm_growl / srm_lock** (SRM selected): keep both loops running from `sndc_init` at the -74 dB floor
  (as snd.cpp does with the engine) so they never restart audibly. Seeker signal `s` 0..1 (target heat in
  the seeker cone, e.g. 1 - angle/gimbal x range factor): growl `vol = 0.65 x db(-6 x (1 - s))`, `pitch = 1 +
  0.25 x s`. On lock: growl to the floor, srm_lock to 0.25 (pitch 1). Lock lost or missile fired: back to the
  growl. No SRM selected: both at the floor. No `lock_beep` for the SRM lock (the tone is the cue).
- **lock_beep**: once when S long designates and the radar lock (STT) is achieved; not on re-locks within 2 s.
- **rwr_lock**: `au_play` at position 0 (loop, vol 0.30) when the first enemy fire-control radar locks the
  player (STT), `au_stop` when no enemy has a lock any more. One voice no matter how many enemies lock.
- **rwr_launch + rwr_missile** (one continuous 455/555 Hz tone, 0.10 s per tone): on the first hostile missile
  homing on the player (11.5 rules: LRM at launch, SRM within 5 km): rwr_launch once (vol 0.45, the same as
  the loop), then `au_play` rwr_missile (loop, position 0, vol 0.45) 0.5 s later. rwr_launch ends on 555 Hz
  at a whole cycle and the loop starts on 455 Hz at phase 0, so a sample-exact start is seamless. au has no
  sample-exact chaining: start the loop when `au_playing(launch voice)` turns 0 or 0.5 s after the launch,
  whichever comes first; both ends sit at a zero crossing, so a frame of gap is a tiny dropout, not a click.
  (Equivalent and simpler: skip rwr_launch and start rwr_missile at once; it sounds the same, only
  starting on 455 Hz.) Stop it when no hostile missile is homing on the player. A second missile while the
  warning runs: **do not** play rwr_launch again (two copies of the alternation out of step would beat);
  the loop keeps going and the anti-fatigue level resets to full. **Anti-fatigue rule**: full volume for
  the first 2 s of a warning, then -4 dB while it persists; back to full when the nearest homing missile is
  < 2 km (TTG short) or a new missile is launched.
- **rwr_search** ("waterfall", vol 0.25): once for every new enemy fighter (airborne-intercept) radar that
  first detects the player (it is added to the threat table); rate-limit to one per 1 s (a second new radar
  within 1 s is not announced again) and never while rwr_lock or rwr_missile play.
- **Stopping continuous tones** (rwr_lock, rwr_missile, srm_lock): the waveform is never silent, so a hard
  `au_stop` mid-cycle can tick; prefer 2-3 frames of falling `au_set` volume (x0.5, x0.25) before `au_stop`.
- **msl_launch**: own launch at the listed volume, pitch 1.0 (LRM) / 1.04 (SRM, a little brighter). Enemy
  launches: positional (vol x min(1, 300 m / d), pan by bearing), usually inaudible beyond 2 km.
- **msl_motor**: one voice per audible missile, nearest 3 only (au pool is 32 voices): `vol = 0.65 x
  min(1, 100 m / d)`, `pitch = clamp(340 / (340 + range_rate), 0.6, 1.6)` (range_rate in m/s, + = opening),
  pan by bearing. Own missiles: fade out over the first 2 s after launch (msl_launch already carries it).
- **msl_pass**: hostile missile that misses within 200 m: trigger 0.45 s before the predicted closest approach
  (or at the miss detection; the 0.45 s lead is just cosmetic), `vol x min(1, 50 m / miss)` floor 0.4.
- **jet_pass**: enemy within 1.5 km closing: trigger when time to closest approach <= 0.6 s and the miss
  distance < 600 m; `vol = 0.90 x min(1, 150 m / miss)`, pitch 0.9-1.1 by closing speed; once per enemy per
  8 s. Distinct from the player's own engine (it glides down through the pass).
- **flare**: once per burst (F; hold repeats every 0.5 s, the file is 0.55 s).
- **hit**: own damage, vol 1.00. **expl_air**: kills and air detonations: 0.95 within 1 km, then x (1 km / d)
  with the sound delayed by d / 340 m/s (A5's `expl_far` for ground/sea impacts and > 4 km). **kill**: 0.35 s
  after the kill (with the SPLASH message), not delayed by distance.
- **no_msl**: on Space with the selected weapon empty.

## Priorities and ducking

1. **PULL UP** (A5) and **rwr_missile / rwr_launch**: never ducked. While PULL UP plays, rwr_missile and
   rwr_launch -3 dB (both, so the joined tone keeps one level).
2. **hit**, **msl_launch** (own), **lock_beep**, **srm_lock**: never ducked; growl and srm_lock never together.
3. **rwr_lock**: muted while rwr_missile plays (the missile warning replaces it).
4. **srm_growl**: -6 dB while rwr_missile plays (you can still hear the seeker find a target).
5. **rwr_search**: skipped while rwr_lock or rwr_missile play (never queued for later).
6. Positional sounds (msl_motor, msl_pass, jet_pass, expl_air, enemy launches): no ducking; on voice
   shortage drop the farthest first. Warning/tone voices are reserved (never stolen).
Group volumes (suggested `[sound]` keys for T17): `warn` (rwr_*, srm_*, lock_beep, no_msl) 1.0, `combat`
(launches, motors, passes, explosions, hit, flare, kill) 1.0.

## Preview

`python3 tools/sfx/gen_sfx_combat.py` also writes `tools/sfx/preview_combat.wav` (44 s, not under `--check`):
A5's engine/wind loops with A5's mix law plus these sounds at exactly the volumes and rules above, master 0.7,
normalised afterwards. Script:

- 0-22 s NORMAL cruise (eng_mil + wind at 480 kt)
- 1.0 rwr_search waterfall (an enemy fighter radar detects us), 2.2 rwr_search (a second fighter)
- 3.0 lock_beep (S long: own radar lock), 5.0 msl_launch (LRM)
- 9.0-13.0 srm_growl: searching floor, then the seeker signal rises (volume up, pitch 1.0 -> 1.25)
- 13.0-14.6 srm_lock (growl replaced), 14.6 msl_launch (SRM; lock tone stops)
- 17.0-21.0 rwr_lock (enemy locks us)
- 21.0 rwr_launch, 21.5-28.4 rwr_missile loop joined sample-exactly: one continuous 455/555 Hz 0.10 s tone from 21.0 (replaces rwr_lock; -4 dB after 2 s, full again near the end)
- 22.0 afterburner (ab_light + eng_ab), 5 g break turn; 24.0/24.5/25.0 flare bursts
- 28.0 msl_pass (the missile misses), warning off
- 30.5-34.5 msl_motor: a stray missile crossing 300 m ahead (distance law + doppler)
- 35.0 jet_pass (closest approach), 37.0 expl_air (our missile's kill, vol x 0.55 for ~2 km; the distance delay is left out), 37.35 kill
- 40.0 hit (we are hit), 43.0 no_msl
